barbell_bench_press.about: The classic horizontal press for chest strength, with the shoulders and triceps helping.
steps: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width, squeeze your shoulder blades together and unrack.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press the bar back up over your shoulders until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your upper back tight and a slight arch; your butt stays on the bench.
Use a spotter or safety arms when going heavy.

incline_barbell_bench_press.about: A bench press on an incline bench that shifts more work to the upper chest and front shoulders.
steps: Set the bench to 30–45° and lie back with your eyes under the bar.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width, pull your shoulder blades back and unrack.
Lower the bar to your upper chest, just below the collarbones.
Press up and slightly back until the bar is over your shoulders.
tips: A lower incline (around 30°) keeps the chest working more than the shoulders.
Don't let your lower back lift off the bench.

decline_barbell_bench_press.about: A bench press on a decline bench that emphasizes the lower chest with a shorter range of motion.
steps: Hook your legs under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack with straight arms.
Lower the bar to your lower chest under control.
Press the bar back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Have a spotter hand you the bar; unracking on a decline is awkward.
Keep your shoulder blades pinched throughout.

close_grip_bench_press.about: A bench press with a narrower grip that loads the triceps more than the chest.
steps: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar about shoulder width apart.
Unrack and hold the bar over your shoulders.
Lower it to your lower chest, keeping elbows close to your sides.
Press back up by straightening your elbows.
tips: Shoulder width is close enough; a very narrow grip strains the wrists.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.

dumbbell_bench_press.about: A flat press with dumbbells that lets each arm work on its own and allows a deeper stretch.
steps: Sit on a flat bench with dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to chest level.
Start with the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing your feet.
Lower them to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45° from your body.
Press them back up until your arms are straight above your chest.
tips: Keep the dumbbells moving in a slight arc, not flaring out wide.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up with them.

incline_dumbbell_press.about: An incline press with dumbbells that targets the upper chest and front shoulders.
steps: Set the bench to 30–45° and sit back with a dumbbell on each thigh.
Kick the dumbbells up to shoulder level as you lie back.
Press them up over your upper chest until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to the sides of your upper chest.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades back and down against the bench.
Avoid clanking the dumbbells at the top; stop just short.

decline_dumbbell_press.about: A decline press with dumbbells that focuses on the lower chest.
steps: Secure your legs on a decline bench and lie back holding dumbbells at your chest.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Lower them under control to the sides of your lower chest.
Press back up, bringing the dumbbells slightly together at the top.
tips: Use moderate weight; getting heavy dumbbells into position on a decline is hard.
Keep your elbows at about 45°.

dumbbell_fly.about: An isolation move that stretches and squeezes the chest with a wide arc.
steps: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells over your chest, palms facing each other.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms out to the sides.
Lower until you feel a stretch across your chest, elbows level with the bench.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest in the same arc.
tips: Keep the elbow bend fixed; this is a hug, not a press.
Use lighter weight than for pressing.

incline_dumbbell_fly.about: A fly on an incline bench that focuses on the upper chest.
steps: Set the bench to about 30° and lie back holding dumbbells over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and open your arms wide.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your upper chest.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
tips: Control the bottom of the movement; don't bounce.
Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.

cable_crossover.about: A standing cable fly that keeps tension on the chest through the whole movement.
steps: Set both pulleys high, take a handle in each hand and step forward.
Lean slightly forward with a small bend in your elbows, arms open wide.
Pull the handles down and together in front of your hips.
Slowly let your arms open back out until you feel a stretch.
tips: Think of squeezing your chest, not pulling with your arms.
Stagger your feet for balance.

low_to_high_cable_fly.about: A cable fly that sweeps upward to target the upper chest.
steps: Set both pulleys low, take a handle in each hand and step forward.
Start with your arms down and slightly behind you, elbows softly bent.
Sweep the handles up and together to about chin height.
Lower them back slowly along the same path.
tips: Keep your chest up and shoulders down.
Pause briefly at the top to squeeze the upper chest.

machine_chest_press.about: A guided chest press that's easy to learn and safe to push hard.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your mid-chest.
Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Press the handles forward until your arms are straight.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch in your chest.
tips: Keep your shoulder blades against the pad.
Don't let the weight stack touch between reps.

pec_deck.about: A machine fly that isolates the chest with a fixed arc.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Sit back and hold the handles or pads with a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your arms together in front of your chest.
Open back out slowly until you feel a stretch.
tips: Keep your chest up and back against the pad.
Avoid letting your shoulders roll forward.

push_up.about: A bodyweight press that works the chest, shoulders, triceps and core.
steps: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows about 45° from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
tips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your hips don't sag.
Make it easier on your knees or with hands on a bench.

incline_push_up.about: A push-up with your hands raised, an easier version that builds up to full push-ups.
steps: Place your hands on a bench or box, a little wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back so your body is in a straight line.
Lower your chest to the edge of the bench.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
tips: The higher the surface, the easier the push-up.
Keep your core tight and hips in line.

chest_dip.about: A dip with a forward lean that loads the lower chest along with the triceps.
steps: Grip the parallel bars and lift yourself up with straight arms.
Lean your torso forward and let your elbows flare slightly.
Lower until your shoulders are just below your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms.
tips: Only go as deep as your shoulders feel comfortable.
Use an assisted dip machine or a band if you can't do bodyweight reps yet.

smith_machine_bench_press.about: A bench press on a guided bar, useful for training hard without a spotter.
steps: Set a flat bench under the bar so it lines up with your mid-chest.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unhook the bar.
Lower it under control to your chest.
Press up until your arms are straight, then hook the bar back.
tips: Set the safety stops just above your chest.
Keep your shoulder blades squeezed together.

deadlift.about: A full-body pull from the floor that builds the back, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Stand with your mid-foot under the bar, feet about hip width apart.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs; shins touch the bar.
Brace your core, flatten your back and push the floor away to stand up.
Lower the bar by pushing your hips back, keeping it close to your legs.
tips: Keep the bar touching your legs the whole way.
Never round your lower back; lower the weight if you can't keep it flat.

barbell_row.about: A bent-over row that builds a thick upper back and strong lats.
steps: Hold the bar with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is about 45° or lower, back flat.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back.
Lower it under control until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your torso still; don't heave the weight up with your hips.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.

pendlay_row.about: A strict row from the floor with a flat back, each rep starting dead.
steps: Set the bar on the floor and hinge until your back is nearly parallel to it.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest.
Lower it back to the floor and reset before the next rep.
tips: Your torso stays parallel to the floor; no standing up.
Let the bar settle on the floor every rep.

t_bar_row.about: A row with one end of the bar anchored, letting you load heavy with a neutral grip.
steps: Straddle the bar and grip the handle or the bar just below the plates.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and slightly bent knees.
Pull the weight toward your chest, elbows close to your body.
Lower it slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your chest up and back flat.
Don't jerk the weight with your lower back.

dumbbell_row.about: A one-arm row supported on a bench that lets each side work on its own.
steps: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, back flat.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with your arm straight down.
Pull the dumbbell to your hip, elbow close to your body.
Lower it slowly until your arm is straight, then switch sides after the set.
tips: Pull with your elbow, not your hand.
Don't twist your torso to lift the weight.

chest_supported_dumbbell_row.about: A row lying face down on an incline bench, taking the lower back out of it.
steps: Set a bench to about 30° and lie face down with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang straight down.
Row both dumbbells up, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower them slowly to the start.
tips: Keep your chest on the pad the whole time.
Pause at the top for a stronger squeeze.

seated_cable_row.about: A seated row on a cable that trains the middle back with constant tension.
steps: Sit at the cable row with your feet on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Grab the handle and sit tall with your arms straight.
Pull the handle to your stomach, driving your elbows back.
Let your arms extend slowly while keeping your back straight.
tips: Don't rock back and forth to move the weight.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of each pull.

lat_pulldown.about: A cable pulldown that builds the lats and helps work toward pull-ups.
steps: Sit with your thighs under the pad and grip the bar wider than your shoulders.
Lean back slightly with your chest up.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving your elbows down.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Pull with your back, not by leaning far back.
Don't pull the bar behind your neck.

close_grip_lat_pulldown.about: A pulldown with a narrow neutral grip that works the lats through a long range.
steps: Attach a close-grip handle and sit with your thighs under the pad.
Hold the handle with palms facing each other and arms straight.
Pull the handle to your upper chest, elbows close to your body.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your chest up toward the handle.
Let your shoulders stretch up at the top of each rep.

straight_arm_pulldown.about: A lat isolation move done with straight arms on a cable.
steps: Attach a bar or rope to a high pulley and stand facing it.
Hinge slightly forward and hold the bar with straight arms at eye level.
Pull the bar down in an arc to your thighs, keeping your arms straight.
Let it rise back slowly to eye level.
tips: Keep a small, fixed bend in your elbows.
Focus on your lats, not your triceps.

pull_up.about: A bodyweight pull that builds the lats, upper back and biceps.
steps: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull your shoulders down and back to start the movement.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
tips: Avoid swinging; keep your legs still.
Use a band or the assisted machine to build up reps.

chin_up.about: A pull-up with palms facing you, putting more work on the biceps.
steps: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder width apart.
Pull your shoulders down and engage your core.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower yourself slowly to a full hang.
tips: Go all the way down each rep.
Keep your body still; no kicking.

assisted_pull_up.about: A pull-up on a machine that takes off part of your bodyweight.
steps: Set the assist weight; more weight means more help.
Kneel or stand on the platform and grip the handles.
Pull yourself up until your chin is over the handles.
Lower yourself slowly to straight arms.
tips: Lower the assistance over time to build toward full pull-ups.
Keep the same strict form as a regular pull-up.

inverted_row.about: A bodyweight row under a bar, a great way to build pulling strength.
steps: Set a bar at about waist height and lie under it.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower yourself until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line like a plank.
Make it easier by bending your knees or raising the bar.

machine_row.about: A guided row with chest support that's easy to push close to failure.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the handles.
Pull the handles back, driving your elbows past your body.
Return slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your chest on the pad.
Pause and squeeze at the back of each rep.

back_extension.about: A hip extension on a bench that strengthens the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Set the pad just below your hips and hook your ankles under the rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest and let your torso hang down.
Raise your torso until your body is in a straight line.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Don't overextend past a straight line at the top.
Hold a plate to your chest to make it harder.

rack_pull.about: A partial deadlift from the safety pins that overloads the top of the pull.
steps: Set the bar on the pins at about knee height.
Stand close with feet hip width apart and grip the bar outside your legs.
Brace and stand up by driving your hips forward.
Lower the bar back to the pins under control.
tips: Keep your back flat and shoulders over the bar at the start.
Don't lean back at the top; just stand tall.

kettlebell_swing.about: An explosive hip hinge that builds the glutes, hamstrings and conditioning.
steps: Stand with feet a bit wider than hips, kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge and hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it up to chest height.
Let it fall back between your legs and go straight into the next rep.
tips: The power comes from your hips, not your arms.
Keep your back flat and stand tall at the top.

dead_hang.about: Hanging from a bar for time to build grip strength and decompress the shoulders.
steps: Grab a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, shoulder width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms.
Keep your shoulders slightly engaged, not fully shrugged up.
Hold for the target time, then step down.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the hold.
Use a box to step up and down safely.

overhead_press.about: A standing barbell press that builds strong shoulders and triceps.
steps: Hold the bar at your collarbones with a grip just outside your shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to clear it.
Lock out overhead, then lower back to your collarbones.
tips: Don't lean back; keep your ribs down.
Push your head through once the bar passes your face.

seated_dumbbell_shoulder_press.about: A seated press with dumbbells that trains each shoulder on its own.
steps: Sit on a bench with an upright back and dumbbells at shoulder height.
Palms face forward, elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to shoulder height.
tips: Keep your back against the pad.
Don't let the dumbbells drift too far forward.

arnold_press.about: A dumbbell press with a rotation that hits all parts of the shoulder.
steps: Sit holding dumbbells at chin height, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating your palms to face forward.
Finish with arms straight overhead.
Reverse the rotation as you lower back to the start.
tips: Make the rotation smooth, not jerky.
Use a little less weight than for a normal press.

machine_shoulder_press.about: A guided overhead press that's easy to learn and push hard.
steps: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Press up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
tips: Keep your back flat against the pad.
Don't lock your elbows hard at the top.

push_press.about: An overhead press helped by a quick dip and drive of the legs, so you can move more weight.
steps: Hold the bar at your collarbones, feet hip width apart.
Dip slightly by bending your knees, keeping your torso upright.
Drive up with your legs and press the bar overhead in one motion.
Lower the bar back to your collarbones.
tips: The dip is short and fast, not a squat.
Finish with the bar over the middle of your feet.

dumbbell_lateral_raise.about: An isolation move for the side of the shoulders that builds width.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides.
Stop at shoulder height.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
tips: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Use light weight and avoid swinging.

cable_lateral_raise.about: A one-arm lateral raise on a cable that keeps tension at the bottom.
steps: Set a pulley low and stand side-on to it.
Grab the handle with the far hand, arm across your body.
Raise your arm out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower slowly and finish the set before switching sides.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbow.
Lean away from the machine a little for a longer range.

machine_lateral_raise.about: A guided lateral raise that isolates the side shoulders.
steps: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot.
Place your arms against the pads.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
tips: Don't shrug your shoulders up.
Control the lowering part of each rep.

dumbbell_front_raise.about: An isolation move for the front of the shoulders.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise one or both arms straight in front of you.
Stop at shoulder height.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Don't lean back to swing the weight up.

reverse_dumbbell_fly.about: A bent-over fly that targets the rear shoulders and upper back.
steps: Hinge forward with a flat back, dumbbells hanging below your chest.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Use light weight; the rear shoulders are small.
Keep your torso still.

reverse_pec_deck.about: A machine fly done in reverse to train the rear shoulders.
steps: Sit facing the pad with the handles set to the rear position.
Grab the handles with arms straight in front of you.
Pull your arms back and out until they're in line with your body.
Return slowly to the front.
tips: Keep your chest against the pad.
Lead with your elbows.

face_pull.about: A rope pull to the face that strengthens the rear shoulders and helps posture.
steps: Set a rope on a cable at head height.
Hold the rope with palms facing each other and step back.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends beside your ears.
Return slowly with control.
tips: Pull your elbows high and back.
Use light weight and focus on the squeeze.

upright_row.about: A barbell pull up the front of the body that works the shoulders and traps.
steps: Hold the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip in front of your thighs.
Pull the bar up close to your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop when the bar reaches lower-chest height.
Lower it slowly back down.
tips: A wider grip is kinder to the shoulders.
Stop at chest height if higher feels pinchy.

band_pull_apart.about: A light band exercise for the rear shoulders, great as a warm-up.
steps: Hold a band in front of you at shoulder height with straight arms.
Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together when the band touches your chest.
Return slowly to the start.
tips: Keep your arms straight.
Use a lighter band for more reps.

kettlebell_press.about: A one-arm overhead press with a kettlebell that also trains stability.
steps: Hold the kettlebell in the rack position at your shoulder.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is straight.
Lower it back to the rack position.
tips: Keep your wrist straight.
Don't lean away from the pressing arm.

barbell_shrug.about: A shrug with a barbell to build the upper traps.
steps: Hold the bar in front of your thighs with a shoulder-width grip.
Stand tall with straight arms.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
tips: Don't roll your shoulders.
Straps help when grip gives out first.

dumbbell_shrug.about: A shrug with dumbbells at your sides to build the upper traps.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Keep your arms straight.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause, then lower slowly.
tips: Move straight up and down; no rolling.
Hold the top for a second each rep.

farmers_carry.about: Walking with heavy weights in each hand to build grip, traps and core.
steps: Pick up a heavy dumbbell in each hand.
Stand tall with shoulders back.
Walk with short, controlled steps for the target time or distance.
Set the weights down carefully.
tips: Don't let the weights pull your shoulders forward.
Keep your core braced while walking.

barbell_curl.about: The classic biceps builder with a straight bar.
steps: Stand holding the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower it slowly until your arms are straight.
tips: Don't swing your body.
Keep your elbows still.

ez_bar_curl.about: A curl with an angled bar that's easier on the wrists.
steps: Hold the EZ-bar on the angled grips, palms up.
Stand tall with elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Control the lowering phase.
Keep your wrists neutral.

dumbbell_bicep_curl.about: A curl with dumbbells that trains each arm on its own.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Keep your elbows close to your body.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Alternate arms or curl both together.
Don't swing your torso.

hammer_curl.about: A curl with a neutral grip that works the biceps and forearms.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up with your thumbs leading.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Keep palms facing each other the whole time.
Don't let your elbows drift forward.

incline_dumbbell_curl.about: A curl lying back on an incline bench that stretches the biceps.
steps: Set a bench to about 45° and lie back holding dumbbells.
Let your arms hang straight down behind your body.
Curl the dumbbells up without moving your upper arms.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.
tips: Keep your upper arms still.
Use lighter weight than standing curls.

preacher_curl.about: A curl with your arms on a pad that stops cheating.
steps: Sit at the preacher bench with the backs of your arms on the pad.
Hold the bar or handles with an underhand grip.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are almost straight.
tips: Don't lift your elbows off the pad.
Control the bottom; don't drop the weight.

concentration_curl.about: A seated one-arm curl braced on your thigh for strict isolation.
steps: Sit on a bench and rest the back of your arm against your inner thigh.
Hold a dumbbell with your arm straight down.
Curl it up toward your shoulder.
Lower it slowly, then switch arms after the set.
tips: Keep your upper arm still.
Squeeze at the top of each rep.

cable_curl.about: A curl on a low cable that keeps tension on the biceps the whole way.
steps: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and stand facing it.
Hold the bar with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Keep your elbows at your sides.
Stand close enough that the cable is vertical.

bayesian_cable_curl.about: A one-arm cable curl facing away from the stack, stretching the biceps hard.
steps: Set a pulley low, take the handle and face away from the machine.
Step forward so your arm is pulled slightly behind your body.
Curl the handle forward and up without moving your upper arm.
Lower slowly back to the stretched position, then switch arms.
tips: Keep your elbow behind your torso.
Use a staggered stance for balance.

band_curl.about: A biceps curl with a resistance band, handy at home or as a finisher.
steps: Stand on the middle of the band and hold the ends, palms up.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl your hands toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Step wider on the band to make it harder.
Control the lowering phase.

triceps_pushdown.about: A cable pushdown that isolates the triceps.
steps: Attach a bar to a high pulley and grip it overhand.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Let it rise slowly until your forearms are about parallel to the floor.
tips: Don't let your elbows drift forward.
Lean slightly forward if it helps you stay steady.

rope_pushdown.about: A pushdown with a rope that lets your hands spread at the bottom.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and hold the ends.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Push down and spread the rope ends apart at the bottom.
Return slowly to the start.
tips: Squeeze your triceps at the bottom.
Keep your upper arms still.

overhead_cable_triceps_extension.about: A triceps extension overhead on a cable that stretches the long head.
steps: Attach a rope to a low or mid pulley and face away from the machine.
Hold the rope behind your head with elbows pointing up.
Extend your arms forward and up until they're straight.
Return slowly to the stretched position.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your head.
Stagger your feet for balance.

overhead_dumbbell_triceps_extension.about: A triceps extension holding one dumbbell overhead.
steps: Hold one dumbbell with both hands under the top plate.
Raise it overhead with straight arms.
Lower it behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend back up to straight arms.
tips: Keep your elbows pointing forward, not flaring out.
Brace your core so your back doesn't arch.

skull_crusher.about: A lying triceps extension with a bar lowered toward the forehead.
steps: Lie on a bench holding an EZ-bar or barbell with straight arms over your chest.
Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead.
Stop just above your forehead or slightly behind your head.
Extend your arms back to the start.
tips: Keep your upper arms still and pointing up.
Use a spotter or start light.

dumbbell_kickback.about: A bent-over triceps isolation move with a dumbbell.
steps: Place one hand and knee on a bench, holding a dumbbell in the other hand.
Bring your upper arm up parallel to the floor.
Extend your arm back until it's straight.
Lower slowly, then switch arms after the set.
tips: Keep your upper arm still.
Use light weight and squeeze at the top.

triceps_dip.about: An upright dip on parallel bars that loads the triceps.
steps: Grip the parallel bars and lift yourself up with straight arms.
Keep your torso upright and elbows close to your body.
Lower until your elbows are bent about 90°.
Press back up to straight arms.
tips: Staying upright keeps the work on the triceps.
Use assistance if you can't do bodyweight reps yet.

bench_dip.about: A dip with your hands on a bench behind you, a simple triceps move.
steps: Sit on a bench, hands beside your hips, and slide your hips off the edge.
Keep your legs bent or straight in front of you.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90°.
Press back up to straight arms.
tips: Keep your back close to the bench.
Don't go too deep if your shoulders feel strained.

machine_triceps_extension.about: A guided triceps extension that's easy to push close to failure.
steps: Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot.
Place your arms on the pad and grip the handles.
Extend your arms until they're straight.
Return slowly to the start.
tips: Keep your back against the pad.
Control the return.

diamond_push_up.about: A push-up with hands close together that targets the triceps.
steps: Get in a plank with your hands together under your chest, forming a diamond.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward your hands.
Push back up to straight arms.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body.
Do them on your knees to make them easier.

wrist_curl.about: A forearm exercise curling the weight up with palms facing up.
steps: Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms up, holding a dumbbell or bar.
Let your wrists hang over your knees.
Curl your wrists up as far as you can.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Only your wrists move.
Use light weight and high reps.

reverse_wrist_curl.about: A forearm exercise curling the wrists up with palms facing down.
steps: Sit with your forearms on your thighs, palms down, holding a dumbbell or bar.
Let your wrists hang over your knees.
Raise the backs of your hands up as far as you can.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Use lighter weight than wrist curls.
Keep your forearms still on your thighs.

reverse_barbell_curl.about: A curl with an overhand grip that works the forearms and biceps.
steps: Hold the bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keep your elbows at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Keep your wrists straight.
An EZ-bar is easier on the wrists.

barbell_back_squat.about: The king of leg exercises, building the quads, glutes and core.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back and step back with feet about shoulder width apart.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Sit down and back until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up.
tips: Keep your knees tracking over your toes.
Use safety bars set just below your bottom position.

front_squat.about: A squat with the bar on the front of your shoulders that loads the quads and keeps you upright.
steps: Rest the bar on your front shoulders with elbows high.
Stand with feet about shoulder width apart.
Squat down keeping your torso upright and elbows up.
Drive back up to standing.
tips: If your wrists are tight, use a cross-arm grip or straps.
Keep your elbows high so the bar doesn't roll forward.

goblet_squat.about: A squat holding a dumbbell at your chest, great for learning good squat form.
steps: Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width.
Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest up.
Stand back up by driving through your feet.
tips: Your elbows can lightly push your knees out at the bottom.
Keep the weight close to your body.

hack_squat.about: A machine squat on an angled sled that targets the quads.
steps: Stand on the platform with your back and shoulders against the pads.
Place your feet about shoulder width apart and release the safety handles.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Push back up without locking your knees hard.
tips: Lower foot placement hits the quads more.
Keep your back against the pad.

smith_machine_squat.about: A squat on a guided bar, steady and easy to control.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back and step your feet slightly forward.
Unhook the bar and brace your core.
Squat down until your thighs are about parallel.
Drive back up and re-hook the bar when done.
tips: Set the safety stops just below your bottom position.
Experiment with foot placement to find what feels best.

leg_press.about: A machine press that loads the legs heavily without needing a barbell.
steps: Sit in the machine and place your feet shoulder width apart on the platform.
Release the safety handles.
Lower the platform until your knees are bent about 90°.
Push back up without locking your knees.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the seat.
Don't let your knees cave in.

leg_extension.about: A machine isolation move for the quads.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the machine's pivot.
Place your ankles under the pad.
Extend your legs until they're straight.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Pause briefly at the top.
Don't swing the weight up.

bulgarian_split_squat.about: A rear-foot elevated split squat that builds the quads and glutes one leg at a time.
steps: Stand a step in front of a bench and place one foot behind you on it.
Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front foot to stand back up, then switch legs after the set.
tips: Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Find a stance where your front knee stays stable.

dumbbell_lunge.about: A stepping lunge with dumbbells for legs and balance.
steps: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs or complete one side first.
tips: Keep your torso upright.
Take a long enough step so your front knee stays over your foot.

walking_lunge.about: Lunges stepping forward continuously, great for legs and conditioning.
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee.
Push off and bring your back foot forward into the next lunge.
Keep walking for the target reps.
tips: Keep your steps steady and controlled.
Look ahead, not down.

barbell_lunge.about: A lunge with a barbell on your back for heavier loading.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back.
Step forward and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through your front foot to return to standing.
Alternate legs.
tips: Start with lighter weight to master balance.
Keep your core braced.

step_up.about: Stepping onto a box with dumbbells for leg strength and balance.
steps: Stand facing a box or bench holding dumbbells.
Place one foot fully on the box.
Drive through that foot to step up.
Step back down under control and repeat.
tips: Push through the top leg; don't spring off the bottom one.
Pick a box height that keeps your knee near 90°.

bodyweight_squat.about: A squat with no added weight, good for warm-ups and building the pattern.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder width apart.
Push your hips back and bend your knees.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Stand back up.
tips: Keep your heels on the floor.
Reach your arms forward for balance.

pistol_squat.about: A one-leg squat that needs strength, balance and mobility.
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg straight out in front.
Squat down on the standing leg, keeping the free leg off the floor.
Lower as far as you can control.
Drive back up to standing.
tips: Hold onto a post or use a box at first.
Keep your heel on the floor.

sissy_squat.about: A knee-forward squat that isolates the quads.
steps: Stand holding onto something for balance.
Rise onto your toes and lean back as you bend your knees forward.
Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your quads.
Return to standing.
tips: Keep your hips, torso and knees in a straight line.
Only go as low as feels comfortable for your knees.

wall_sit.about: Holding a seated position against a wall to build quad endurance.
steps: Stand with your back against a wall.
Slide down until your knees are bent about 90°.
Keep your back flat against the wall.
Hold for the target time.
tips: Keep your knees over your ankles.
Breathe steadily during the hold.

kettlebell_goblet_squat.about: A goblet squat holding a kettlebell by the horns.
steps: Hold a kettlebell by the handle at your chest.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder width.
Squat down keeping your chest up.
Stand back up through your whole foot.
tips: Keep the kettlebell close to your chest.
Go as deep as your form allows.

romanian_deadlift.about: A hip hinge with a barbell that builds the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Hold the bar at your hips with an overhand grip.
With a slight bend in your knees, push your hips back.
Lower the bar along your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.
tips: Keep your back flat and the bar close to your legs.
The movement is in your hips, not your knees.

dumbbell_romanian_deadlift.about: A Romanian deadlift with dumbbells for the hamstrings and glutes.
steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
With knees slightly bent, push your hips back.
Lower the dumbbells along your legs to below your knees.
Drive your hips forward to stand up.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings.

stiff_leg_deadlift.about: A deadlift with straighter legs for a deeper hamstring stretch.
steps: Hold the bar with an overhand grip.
Keep your legs nearly straight.
Hinge at the hips and lower the bar toward the floor.
Stand back up by driving your hips forward.
tips: Only lower as far as you can keep your back flat.
Use lighter weight than a regular deadlift.

lying_leg_curl.about: A machine curl lying face down that isolates the hamstrings.
steps: Lie face down with your ankles under the pad.
Grip the handles to stay steady.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly back down.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the pad.
Don't let the weight drop.

seated_leg_curl.about: A machine curl sitting down that trains the hamstrings in a stretched position.
steps: Adjust the seat so your knees line up with the pivot.
Place your lower calves on the pad and lock the thigh pad down.
Curl your legs down and back.
Return slowly.
tips: Lean slightly forward for a better stretch.
Control the return.

good_morning.about: A barbell hip hinge with the bar on your back for the hamstrings and lower back.
steps: Set the bar on your upper back like a squat.
With a slight knee bend, push your hips back.
Lower your torso until it's nearly parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward to stand up.
tips: Start very light.
Keep your back flat throughout.

nordic_hamstring_curl.about: A bodyweight exercise lowering yourself forward against your hamstrings.
steps: Kneel with your ankles secured under something sturdy.
Keep your body straight from knees to head.
Lower yourself forward as slowly as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up.
tips: Focus on the slow lowering.
Use a band for assistance at first.

sumo_deadlift.about: A deadlift with a wide stance and hands inside the legs.
steps: Stand with a wide stance and toes pointed out.
Grip the bar inside your legs.
Push your knees out and drive through the floor to stand up.
Lower the bar back down under control.
tips: Keep your chest up.
Push your knees out over your toes.

trap_bar_deadlift.about: A deadlift with a hex bar that's easier on the back and great for beginners.
steps: Step inside the trap bar and grip the handles.
Hinge with a flat back and bent knees.
Drive through the floor to stand up.
Lower the bar back down.
tips: Keep your back flat.
Push through your whole foot.

barbell_hip_thrust.about: A hip extension with a barbell that builds the glutes.
steps: Sit with your upper back against a bench and the bar over your hips.
Plant your feet flat, about shoulder width apart.
Drive your hips up until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Lower your hips back down.
tips: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down.
Use a pad on the bar for comfort.

glute_bridge.about: A bodyweight hip lift on the floor that trains the glutes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes.
Pause at the top.
Lower back down.
tips: Push through your heels.
Don't overarch your lower back.

cable_kickback.about: A cable exercise kicking one leg back to isolate the glutes.
steps: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley.
Face the machine and hold on for support.
Kick your strapped leg straight back.
Return slowly, then switch legs after the set.
tips: Keep your hips square.
Squeeze your glute at the top.

hip_abduction_machine.about: A machine pushing the legs apart to train the outer glutes.
steps: Sit in the machine with the pads on the outside of your knees.
Push your legs apart as far as you can.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly.
tips: Control the return.
Lean slightly forward to hit the glutes more.

hip_adduction_machine.about: A machine squeezing the legs together to train the inner thighs.
steps: Sit in the machine with the pads on the inside of your knees.
Squeeze your legs together.
Pause briefly.
Return slowly.
tips: Don't let the weights slam.
Keep your back against the pad.

cable_pull_through.about: A hip hinge pulling a cable between your legs for the glutes and hamstrings.
steps: Attach a rope to a low pulley and face away from the machine.
Hold the rope between your legs.
Hinge forward, then drive your hips forward to stand up.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
tips: The movement comes from your hips.
Keep your arms straight.

standing_calf_raise.about: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
steps: Stand on the edge of a step or calf machine.
Lower your heels below the step.
Rise up onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Pause at the top and bottom.
Use a full range of motion.

seated_calf_raise.about: A seated calf raise that focuses on the soleus.
steps: Sit with the pad over your knees and the balls of your feet on the platform.
Lower your heels down.
Raise your heels as high as you can.
Lower slowly.
tips: Use a full range.
Don't bounce.

steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Stand on a step with your heels hanging off.
Rise up onto your toes.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Hold on with one hand for balance if needed.
Pause at the top.

leg_press_calf_raise.about: A calf raise on the leg press machine.
steps: Sit in the leg press with the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Keep your legs almost straight.
Push the platform away with your toes.
Return slowly.
tips: Don't lock your knees.
Use a full range of motion.

plank.about: A static hold that builds core strength and stability.
steps: Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows under your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Hold for the target time.
tips: Don't let your hips sag or rise.
Breathe steadily throughout.

side_plank.about: A side hold that trains the obliques and lateral core.
steps: Lie on your side and prop yourself up on one forearm.
Stack your feet and lift your hips off the floor.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Hold for the target time, then switch sides.
tips: Keep your hips lifted.
Bend your bottom knee to make it easier.

crunch.about: A simple ab exercise curling the upper body toward the knees.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands lightly behind your head or across your chest.
Curl your shoulders off the floor.
Lower back down slowly.
tips: Don't pull on your neck.
Focus on squeezing your abs.

cable_crunch.about: A kneeling crunch with a cable for weighted ab training.
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing it.
Hold the rope beside your head.
Crunch down, bringing your elbows toward your knees.
Return slowly.
tips: Curl your spine; don't just bend at the hips.
Keep your hips still.

hanging_leg_raise.about: Raising straight legs while hanging, a hard core exercise.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Keep your legs straight.
Raise your legs until they're parallel to the floor or higher.
Lower slowly.
tips: Avoid swinging.
Bend your knees to make it easier.

hanging_knee_raise.about: Raising the knees while hanging, an easier version of the leg raise.
steps: Hang from a bar with straight arms.
Bring your knees up toward your chest.
Curl your pelvis up slightly at the top.
Lower slowly.
tips: Control the movement.
Don't swing.

lying_leg_raise.about: Raising the legs while lying on your back to train the lower abs.
steps: Lie on your back with legs straight.
Place your hands under your hips for support.
Raise your legs until they're vertical.
Lower slowly without touching the floor.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed down.
Bend your knees slightly if needed.

ab_wheel_rollout.about: Rolling an ab wheel forward and back for strong core control.
steps: Kneel holding the ab wheel under your shoulders.
Roll the wheel forward, extending your body.
Go as far as you can while keeping your back flat.
Roll back to the start.
tips: Keep your core tight.
Don't let your lower back sag.

russian_twist.about: A seated twist that trains the obliques.
steps: Sit with knees bent and lean back slightly.
Hold a weight or clasp your hands.
Rotate your torso to one side.
Rotate to the other side.
tips: Move from your torso, not just your arms.
Lift your feet to make it harder.

pallof_press.about: An anti-rotation press on a cable that trains core stability.
steps: Set a cable at chest height and stand side-on to it.
Hold the handle at your chest with both hands.
Press the handle straight out in front of you.
Hold, then return to your chest; switch sides after the set.
tips: Resist the cable pulling you around.
Keep your hips square.

dead_bug.about: A core exercise on your back moving opposite arm and leg.
steps: Lie on your back with arms up and knees bent at 90°.
Lower one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start.
Repeat on the other side.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Move slowly.

mountain_climber.about: A fast core and cardio move driving the knees in a plank.
steps: Start in a high plank.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly.
Keep alternating.
tips: Keep your hips low.
Go at a pace you can control.

hollow_body_hold.about: A gymnastics hold that builds deep core strength.
steps: Lie on your back with arms overhead.
Lift your shoulders and legs off the floor.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Hold for the target time.
tips: Bend your knees to make it easier.
Keep your lower back down.

power_clean.about: An explosive lift from the floor to the shoulders for power and strength.
steps: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and grip just outside your legs.
Lift the bar off the floor with a flat back.
Explode upward with your hips and shrug.
Catch the bar on your shoulders in a quarter squat.
tips: Learn it with light weight or an empty bar first.
The power comes from your hips.

clean_and_jerk.about: An Olympic lift taking the bar from the floor to overhead in two movements.
steps: Clean the bar to your shoulders.
Dip slightly with your knees.
Drive the bar overhead and split your feet.
Stand up with the bar locked out.
tips: Learn from a qualified coach.
Start with light weights.

snatch.about: An Olympic lift taking the bar from the floor to overhead in one movement.
steps: Grip the bar wide.
Lift it off the floor with a flat back.
Explode upward and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch it overhead in a squat, then stand up.
tips: This is a technical lift; learn from a coach.
Start with a PVC pipe or empty bar.

thruster.about: A front squat flowing into an overhead press, a full-body move.
steps: Hold the bar at your shoulders in a front rack.
Squat down.
Drive up and use the momentum to press the bar overhead.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders.
tips: Make it one smooth movement.
Keep your elbows high in the squat.

kettlebell_turkish_get_up.about: A slow movement from lying to standing with a kettlebell overhead.
steps: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight up in one hand.
Roll onto your elbow, then your hand.
Bridge your hips up and sweep your leg under you to kneel.
Stand up, then reverse the steps to lie back down.
tips: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell.
Start with very light weight or none at all.

burpee.about: A full-body conditioning move: squat, plank, push-up and jump.
steps: From standing, squat down and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a plank.
Do a push-up, then jump your feet back to your hands.
Jump up with your arms overhead.
tips: Keep a steady pace.
Skip the push-up or jump to make it easier.
